accessibility.summary: Per the official Cubs accessibility guide: 'Accessible seating sections are located throughout the ballpark near an elevator, lift and/or ramp.' The guide does NOT publish a list of accessible section numbers - placement is defined by proximity to the seven elevators/ramps. 'Guests with mobility disabilities and up to three companions are encouraged to make their purchase in advance' (i.e., up to 3 companion seats), by phone, email, in person at the Ticket Office, or online. All gates have accessible routes with dedicated accessible lanes; guests enter through their ticketed gate. Complimentary wheelchair escort from gate to seat is first-come, first-served (no reservations); attendants issue a pickup ticket for postgame retrieval. Accessible golf-cart shuttle runs from the Toyota Camry Lot to the Left Field Gate from 3 hours before through 1 hour after games; free remote accessible parking at 4650 N. Clarendon Ave. Service animals may exit and re-enter through the Gallagher Way Gate for relief. A Sensory Room is on the main concourse beside Fan Services behind home plate.

discovery.row_seat_conventions: ROWS ARE NUMBERS at Wrigley, not letters, in essentially all baseball seating: lower Club Box rows 1-15; Field Box (100 level) rows 1-15; Terrace (200 level) rows 1-6 = Terrace Box and rows 7 through ~28-30 = Terrace Reserved; Upper Box (300 level) rows ~1-12; Upper Reserved (400 level) rows ~1-9; Bleachers rows 1-21 (rows only matter in the postseason, when the bleachers switch from GA to assigned). LETTERS appear as SECTION prefixes/suffixes rather than rows: 'AA13'-'AA22' for the 1914 Club, and 'L'/'R' suffixes on 300- and 400-level sections (L = third-base half, R = first-base half). SEAT NUMBERING: RateYourSeats' individual section pages state 'When looking towards the field, lower number seats are on the left,' but its Wrigley seating-chart overview page states the opposite ('the lowest number (typically seat 1) will be on the far right of the section'). These two statements conflict, so the seat-1 side is UNCERTAIN and should be verified against the Cubs 3D Virtual Venue before relying on it. Lower infield sections behind home plate hold roughly 20 seats per row; bleacher rows vary from about 10 to 30 seats.
discovery.known_obstructions: Wrigley is a 1914 ballpark with a steel-post upper-deck structure, and support posts/beams are its signature obstruction problem. Specifics: (1) TERRACE / 200 LEVEL - rows 1-6 (the 'Terrace Box' rows) are the only pole-free rows; from about row 7 back through the 'Terrace Reserved' rows, support poles intrude. Fan reports from section 217 include 'I could not see 3rd base or the video board in left field because of the support pole' (row 19) and 'The poles are right on the aisle' (row 6), forcing fans to squeeze past. (2) 400 LEVEL / UPPER RESERVED - 'All Upper Reserved sections have poles that create obstructed views... Obstructions vary by seat. The only unobstructed row is Row 1' (and row 1 sits on a walkway with foot traffic). (3) 300 LEVEL / UPPER BOX - largely clean: 'Sections 303-331 will be free of obstructions and have a great view.' (4) Roof/overhang - the coverage that shades the 200 and 400 levels comes from the same beam structure causing the obstructions, and the very back rows of the upper deck sit under the press-box overhang, cutting off fly balls. (5) Back of the lower deck also has obstructed sightlines under the Terrace overhang. (6) Some tickets are explicitly sold as 'obstructed view.' The Cubs' 3D Virtual Venue is the recommended way to check a specific seat. CONFIRMED - https://www.rateyourseats.com/wrigley-field/seating/sections/217 , https://www.rateyourseats.com/wrigley-field/seating/sections/420 , https://www.rateyourseats.com/wrigley-field/seating/sections/310 , https://www.rateyourseats.com/wrigley-field/seating/shaded-covered-seats , https://thestadiuminsiders.com/stadium_guides/wrigley-field/ticketing-seating-premium/

sections.notes: The venue index links every lettered Field section to a single shared zone page for Field Seats rather than to a per-section page, so no row, entrance-row, seats-per-row or seat-numbering detail is published for this identifier. The zone is temporary floor seating installed on the playing surface for concerts: "Seats are foldable chairs that are brought in and set up for each show." "Without any elevation between rows it can be more difficult to see if there is a taller person in front of you." Ticket holders receive "wristbands in the outfield near the bleachers. Beer and merchandise tents will be set up on the field for fans to purchase." "The restrooms in the bleachers are used for fans seated on the floor."

sections.location: "Standing Room Only areas are located behind the 200-level sections along the walkways at Wrigley Field." Ticketholders "will be permitted to stand on the walkway behind the Terrace seats."
sections.seat_direction: UNKNOWN
sections.notes: A zone page rather than a section page; there is no assigned seating and no reserved spot, so no rows, entrance row or seat numbering exist. Views are obstructed: "Sightlines are obstructed by the poles supporting the upper deck and by the overhang which covers the Terrace level," with the overhang particularly limiting visibility of flyballs and popups; fans can move along the walkway to avoid standing directly behind a pole. The page describes these as "one of the only ways to get into sold-out or high-demand games," suited to fans who prioritise getting into the ballpark over view quality.

sections.location: "The Executive Club is located on the suite level down the third base line." "Positioned between the lower and upper seating bowls, offering elevated views of the field."
sections.seat_direction: UNKNOWN
sections.notes: A zone page for the club area rather than a per-section page, and it does not name the numbered sections the club covers, so no row, entrance-row, seats-per-row or seat-numbering detail is published. An all-inclusive premium area with "All-inclusive food options and chef-attended selections" and "Beer, wine, cocktails, and nonalcoholic beverages," "Heated indoor seating and climate-controlled comfort" and "padded indoor and outdoor seats." Access runs "two hours before first pitch (90 minutes for 6:40 starts) and one hour after the game." Sold to "fans seeking a suite-level experience with upscale amenities and premium comfort," including early-season and postseason games and groups wanting a more exclusive social setting. Views are described as "unobstructed views of key stadium features, including the ivy walls and scoreboard."
